title: Ultrasound-assisted chelation of whey protein isolates with iron: Effects of power variation on protein conformation and binding efficacy - ScienceDirect
abstract:
Ultrasonic intervention in UWPI-Fe chelation: a novel strategy for effective iron supplementation. ... Ultrasonic power regulates the iron binding ability of WPI and the surface iron valence state of UWPI-Fe. ... UWPI-Fe is a high-quality iron source with high solubility and bioavailability. It is widely recognized that whey protein possesses a mineral-binding capacity that enhances dietary iron absorption, and Ultrasound is a non-thermal physical modification technique that can induce changes in protein conformation.
Consequently, they evolved into organic forms such as ferrous fumarate, which enhanced iron absorption and reduced side effects (Faller et al., 2012; Zhao et al., 2017). Recent studies have focused on developing improved iron supplements to overcome the limitations of conventional options. Protein‑iron chelates, a novel type of iron supplements, have garnered interest owing to their high bioavailability, safety profile, and minimal adverse effects, providing promising candidates for iron supplementation.
Second, the iron chelation capacity and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) were utilized to explore the iron-binding capability of the modified WPI and the distribution and valence states of surface-bound Fe2+. Finally, to validate the potential of the samples as functional food ingredients, we determined their solubility and then subjected them to an in vitro simulated gastrointestinal digestion system to evaluate the effects of different ultrasonic power levels on iron bioavailability. Whey protein isolate (WPI 90, Fonterra Corporation, New Zealand) and analytical grade chemicals were used in this study. In particular, the constituents of the WPI are tabulated in the Supplementary Information as shown in Table S1. Ferrous sulfate heptahydrate (FeSO4·7H2O, CAS 13463–43-9) was sourced from Beijing Chemical Plant (China).

They also exhibit potent mineral-binding (Gandhi et al., 2019) and antioxidant properties (Wei et al., 2024).
